API reference / @jsprismarine/minecraft

JSPrismarine/minecraft ​

This package contains data directly related to the Minecraft: Bedrock Edition game.

Note: This is still a WIP

Why was it introduced? ​

This package is introduced for its convenience in further separating the server logic from the protocol. Previously, importing the server logic was necessary to use the protocol package. However, this idea is particularly compelling for two main reasons:

  • Now, we can directly generate/manage block states or other resources with this package.
  • It effectively separates the game structures from the server logic, resulting in improved modularity and easier maintainability.

Enumerations ​

AbilityLayerFlag ​

Defined in: generated/unversioned/AbilityLayerFlag.ts:19

AbilityLayerFlag, from Mojang's published protocol documentation.

Generated - do not edit. Change datagen/manifest.json and run pnpm generate. Source: Mojang/bedrock-protocol-docs@0e00fe80f4f3c71572ff6429de40146d1f4412fc (Minecraft 1.26.40, protocol 2168) Upstream name: AbilitiesIndex

NOT VERSIONED. No bedrock-protocol-docs release describes this enum: a schema exists only for a type some packet field is declared with, and this one travels as a plain integer. The members below come from the last enums.html Mojang published, for Minecraft 1.26.40, and every protocol this package generates reads them unchanged: 2193, 2225.

Treat them as approximate above protocol 2168. A member added since then is missing, and a member removed since then is still here. No source this package will take numbers from publishes this enum per version, so that is a known gap and not something to correct in the generated file.

Generated - do not edit. Change datagen/manifest.json and run pnpm generate. Source: Mojang/bedrock-protocol-docs@0e00fe80f4f3c71572ff6429de40146d1f4412fc (Minecraft 1.26.40, protocol 2168) Upstream name: LevelEvent

NOT VERSIONED. No bedrock-protocol-docs release describes this enum: a schema exists only for a type some packet field is declared with, and this one travels as a plain integer. The members below come from the last enums.html Mojang published, for Minecraft 1.26.40, and every protocol this package generates reads them unchanged: 2193, 2225.

Treat them as approximate above protocol 2168. A member added since then is missing, and a member removed since then is still here. No source this package will take numbers from publishes this enum per version, so that is a known gap and not something to correct in the generated file.

Known to be wrong:

Incomplete above 2168. ParticleCreakingHeartTrail = 9816 was added in protocol 766, which the 1.26.40 dump lacks, so it is added by hand under rules. Mojang's changelog records four more, SoundPaintingPlace 9817 through CauldronDyeShulkerBox 9820, which were removed again at 1.26.60-preview.30. They are not members of this enum, because they are not current values at any protocol it serves.

ALL_PLAYERS_SLEEPING = 3617, DEPRECATED = 3618 and _9800 = 3619 are the numbers the 1.26.40 dump printed, and they are list positions rather than values: gophertunnel reads the same three as AllPlayersSleeping = 9800 and SleepingPlayers = 9801. Nothing in this repository sends any of the three, and guessing which source is right is not something this file may do.
